question: A 35-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-week history of abdominal cramps, vomiting, and constipation. He also reports having to urinate frequently and occasional leg pain. He has had similar episodes in the past. He has hypertension and peptic ulcer disease. Current medications include captopril and ranitidine. He appears depressed. Physical examination shows weakness in the extremities. Abdominal examination shows mild epigastric tenderness. There is no rebound or guarding. He has a restricted affect. Laboratory studies show elevated serum parathyroid hormone levels; serum calcium is 14.2 mg/dL. Abdominal ultrasonography shows multiple small calculi in the right kidney. Which of the following is most likely to provide rapid relief in this patient?

options.opb: Reduction of dietary intake of calcium
options.opc: Normal saline and intravenous furosemide therapy
options.opd: Normal saline and intravenous fentanyl therapy
options.ope: Normal saline and intravenous calcitonin therapy

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Elevated serum calcium" -> "possible hypercalcemia symptoms" -> "abdominal cramps, vomiting, constipation" -> "frequent urination and leg pain" -> "likely due to kidney stones" -> "normal saline and intravenous furosemide therapy" -> "increased urine output" -> "rapid relief of symptoms" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Elevated serum parathyroid hormone" -> "increased calcium release from bones" -> "hypercalcemia" -> "kidney stones formation" -> "abdominal pain and vomiting" -> "normal saline and intravenous furosemide therapy" -> "promotes calcium excretion" -> "rapid relief of symptoms" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient has hypertension and peptic ulcer disease" -> "current medications include captopril and ranitidine" -> "risk of renal impairment" -> "elevated calcium levels" -> "normal saline and intravenous furosemide therapy" -> "helps manage hypercalcemia" -> "rapid relief of symptoms" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with weakness in extremities" -> "possible electrolyte imbalance" -> "elevated calcium levels" -> "normal saline and intravenous furosemide therapy" -> "increases renal excretion of calcium" -> "rapid relief of symptoms" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of similar episodes" -> "likely recurrent hypercalcemia" -> "elevated serum calcium" -> "normal saline and intravenous furosemide therapy" -> "effective in treating acute hypercalcemia" -> "rapid relief of symptoms" -> 88%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms consistent with hypercalcemia, likely due to primary hyperparathyroidism, given the elevated parathyroid hormone levels and high serum calcium. The most effective and rapid treatment for symptomatic hypercalcemia is hydration with normal saline and the use of a loop diuretic like furosemide to promote calcium excretion. Other options, such as bisphosphonates or calcitonin, are more appropriate for longer-term management or in cases of malignancy-related hypercalcemia. Therefore, normal saline and intravenous furosemide therapy is the best choice for immediate relief.
